name: inline
title: Launcher action, in line: a pusher between two curved arms shaped by the beam solver, a flooded frame, the disc flat in a roofed slot, the pull ring on top, a solid trigger that is its own sear on a hinge carrying the pull, printed in one piece on its side
orientation: On its side, as drawn: one piece, no supports. Put a finger through the ring and pull it back until it clicks: the pusher slides straight back between the arms, and the tooth under the stem rides over the trigger's hook and catches. Let go of the ring, then pull the trigger back with a finger in the crook in front of it: the hook slides off the tooth and the pusher throws the disc.

body.label: The action: frame, arms and pusher in one print

height_min.rule: The least it may print, on its side: tall enough that the frame and the pusher don't bend out of their plane

height_max.rule: The most it may print: the shaping prints it as tall as it must be, between these, to store the energy (an arm's force goes as its height; its strain doesn't)

gap.rule: The least gap between parts printed in place that still prints apart

slide.rule: The disc's gap each side in its barrel: what slid best on the fit test plate

fit.rule: The pusher's room in its pocket and barrel, each side: the fit test's sliding gap and a little more, so it doesn't drag

room.rule: The arms' room each side, round wherever they go: more than the print gap, so they don't drag on the frame

spring_clear.rule: The arms' room each side: more than the print gap, so the frame is clear of them however they really bend

stroke.rule: How far the tab pulls the pusher back to draw it

short.rule: The ring is drawn this much short of the stroke the arms were shaped for: the frame stops the pusher a sliding gap past the draw, within the arms' finite-element limit

energy.rule: What the spring stores drawn: the launcher's stored energy

safety.rule: The arms' strain limit is PETG's strength over its modulus (its yield strain) over this

margin.rule: The arms are shaped to this share of the strain limit, so the finite-element peak (rounds and all) has room

least.rule: The thinnest an arm may get: three lines (two-line flexures flexed and twisted in the flat action's print)

most.rule: The thickest an arm may get

arm_gap.rule: How far apart an arm's own loops keep: more than the print gap, so they print apart and don't slap together when it fires

arm_bend.rule: The tightest an arm may curve, in its thicknesses: tighter, its inside takes much more strain than beam theory says

legs.rule: The arms start from a meander of this many legs folded into their room (odd), and the shaping moves every point and thickness from there

bend_lo.rule: Where the starting meander's low bends turn, above the axis

evaluations.rule: How many shapes the shaping may try

bar.rule: The pusher bar's height: solid, so it doesn't bend (the flat action's windowed bar did)

bar_back.rule: The bar behind where the arms meet it

bar_front.rule: The bar ahead of where the arms meet it, to its nose

nose_w.rule: The nose's height in the plane: it pushes the flat disc's edge

nose.rule: The pusher's nose: as thick as the disc, forward from the bar between the rails to the disc

rise.rule: The arms' room, from the bar's top to the frame's inside

reach.rule: How far behind where they meet the bar the arms' room reaches

room_front.rule: The arms' room ends here, along the barrel: the disc's slot is ahead of it

root_x.rule: Where each arm grows from the frame, behind where it meets the bar: so the arms pull on the closed back of the frame, not its front

wall.rule: The frame round the arms' room, and the blocks they grow from

least_frame.rule: The thinnest the flooded frame may be anywhere: thinner bits are left out

band.rule: The frame is solid this far round everything that moves and the outline's edge; the rest is windows, so it's a web, light but as stiff where it guides and stops

stem_h.rule: The stem's height in the plane: stout, full height, no bridge over it

ring_x.rule: The pull ring's centre: it stands on the stem, at the front of the room above it, just behind the arms

guide_depth.rule: The ridge on the stem's sides that runs in a groove in the handle, at the middle of the print's height, flanks at 45°

bridge_foot.rule: How far the roof (and a guide's strip) stands on the frame either side of what it spans

bridge_gap.rule: The gap between the disc and the roof over its slot, in layers

roof_span.rule: The widest the roof over the disc's slot may bridge: the X1C bridges this far, by the user's judgement (the rule's 5 mm is cautious), to be proved on the print

ring_in.rule: The pull ring's hole: a finger through it

handle.rule: Solid behind the drawn ring and stem: the handle

into.rule: How far an arm runs on into the wall and the bar, so they join solidly

spring_round.rule: The round where each arm meets the wall and the bar

tooth.rule: The catch's tooth: how far it hangs below the stem

tooth_x.rule: The tooth's front at rest: under the stem, just behind the arms' room

tooth_w.rule: The tooth's length along the barrel: it carries the pull over this and the print's height; short, so the hook has room to be solid

engage.rule: How deep the sear's head reaches up the tooth's face: more than the print gap, so it holds for sure, and little, so the trigger slides it off easily

settle.rule: Let go of, the pusher comes forward this much from the draw on to the sear

sear_reach.rule: The hinge's middle is this far behind the tooth's face: the further, the less the sear turns to let go, the less its hinge bends

sear_drop.rule: and this far below the middle of where the tooth bears: the hook's faces are square to the line from one to the other, so the spring's pull runs straight through the hinge

hinge.rule: The sear's hinge: one straight flexure on that line, the pull in tension along it; the trigger turns it about its middle, where it bends round evenly

hinge_round.rule: The round where the hinge meets the frame and the sear

hinge_least.rule: The thinnest the hinge may be: three lines; it carries the pull in tension, which a strip carries easily, and thinner it's lighter to turn

hinge_swing.rule: How far from the pull's line the shaping may turn the hinge's ends

hinge_room.rule: How far below the hinge's middle the shaping may take it

hinge_energy.rule: What the hinge stores with the trigger pulled: enough to bring the sear back up behind the tooth smartly

hold_design.rule: The pull the hinge is shaped to carry: five times this spring's, for the stronger springs to come

hold_give.rule: The most the hinge may give along the pull's line under it: a fraction of the catch's engagement

hinge_evaluations.rule: How many shapes the hinge's shaping may try

head.rule: The hook's flat top, ahead of its hooked face; its ramp runs on from there down to the trigger's front

chamfer.rule: The hook's and the tooth's meeting corners taken off this much, so they slide past each other as it's drawn

trigger_front.rule: The trigger's top reaches forward to here, just behind the arms' room

trigger_neck.rule: Its front runs straight down this far from its top, then curves back to its toe

trigger_toe.rule: Its toe, on the frame's bottom: the crook in front of the curve is the finger's

trigger_heel.rule: Its heel, behind: the trigger is solid from the toe to here

heel_h.rule: The heel's height, up from the bottom

trigger_waist.rule: Its back runs up from the heel to this far behind the hinge's tip, under the hinge

hinge_clear.rule: The trigger's back keeps this far below the hinge's line: its thickness, its round and room

trigger_round.rule: Every outside corner of the trigger rounded to this: nothing for a finger to catch on

crook.rule: How deep the hollow the finger sits in is, bowed back from a straight line

crook_steps.rule: Steps the hollow is drawn in

trigger_room.rule: The trigger's room in the frame, all round: a hinge doesn't turn quite about one point, so a little more than the print gap; the frame behind it is its stop

finger_wall.rule: The frame left between the finger's room and the arms' room

finger_round.rule: The finger's room's corners rounded to this

finger_at.rule: Where on the crook's face, up from the toe, the finger pulls

pull.rule: How far the trigger turns pulled right back, where the frame behind it stops it (it lets go before)

friction.rule: Friction between printed PETG faces in the simulation: the trigger pulls against it

plate_pin.rule: The snap pins' diameter (objects/pin) that would hold a plate either side: the frame needn't have them

plate_hole.rule: The holes for them through the frame's corners: the pin and the fit test's pin gap round it

plate_in.rule: How far each hole's centre is in from the frame's edges

plate_wall.rule: Solid frame round each hole, however the web falls

round.rule: Every inside corner of the frame and the pusher rounded to this
